title: Nine Princes in Yander
html:
Nine Princes in Yander is a fantasy novel and the first in the Chronicles of Yander series by the late Charli Derevanny. It was first published in 1970.


Plot Summary[]

Carl Corey awakes in a medical clinic, with little to no knowledge of who he is or how he got there. He suspects he is being over-medicated, so he overpowers the nurse and security guard and escapes his room. He finds the manager of the clinic, and learns that he was recovering from a car accident in a private clinic at the expense of his sister, Evelyn Flaumel.

He flees and heads to the house of his sister, who addresses him as Pavel and calls herself Flora. Hiding his lack of knowledge about what she is saying, he convinces her to let him stay. In Flora's library he locates a set of customised tarot cards - the Trumps - whose Major Arcana are replaced with images which he recognises as his family. As he looks over the cards he remembers all his brothers and sisters: sneaky Random, Robert the hunter, well-built Gérard, the arrogant Kripke, himself, Peter the master tactician and swordsman, sinister Avel, scheming Bleys, and the mysterious Jon. He also views his four sisters: Flora who offered him sanctuary, Deirdre who was dear to him, reserved Ciwilla, and Shriona whom Pavel hated.

His brother Random contacts him via telephone and Pavel promises to give him protection. Random arrives, pursued by mysterious spined, bloodshot-eyed humuanoid creatures, and the combined efforts of Pavel, Random, and Flora's dogs ultimately defeat them. Random then asks Pavel whether he wishes to walk the road to Yander, from which Pavel agrees, despite the fact he does not know what he is doing. The world changes around them, and Pavel realises that Random is somehow causing the changes in order for them to proceed to Yander. They ultimately end up in the Forest of Losiniy, the territory of their brother Robert. Robert's beasts confront Random and Pavel and eventually Robert himself appears on his steed Inagentiy to take them himself. Pavel dismounts Robert and takes him prisoner. After taking information from Robert he lets him live, saving himself from the remainder of Robert's men who were awaiting Pavel in the forest. While traveling they encounter Pavel's sister Deirdre who reveals she fled from Kripke's court. Fully confused at this point, Pavel reveals that he has no memory of what they have been doing or of who he is so Deirdre convinces him to walk the Pattern, which she believes will restore his memory.

The three then travel to Rebma, a reflection of Yander underwater, and there they meet their sister Ciwilla and Muira, the queen of Rebma. Muira originally believes that the three of them came to Rebma to seek support to defeat Kripke but Deirdre explains their true intentions. Due to the fact that Rebma is a reflection of Yander, there is also a reflection of the Pattern in Rebma, which Pavel is to walk to restore his memory. Although Random is impounded for past crimes in Rebma and sentenced to wed a blind girl named Vialle, Pavel convinces the queen Muira to allow him to walk the Pattern. After receiving advice from Random and Deirdre, he walks the Pattern, reliving all of his past life, which stretches back to his time in Yander and when Kripke deposited him in Elizabethan England on our Earth. He remembers the powers which his heritage and the Pattern grant him - the power to walk through shadow, and to pronounce a powerful curse before dying. After he completes the Pattern he uses its power to project himself into the Castle of Yander, from which he finds a safe spot and rests.

Afterwards he searches the castle and in the library finds a pack of the Trumps and also an old servant friend. However, Kripke finds them and the two begin to duel. Although intimidated at first by Kripke's immense skill, Pavel gets the upper hand in the fight and injures Kripke on the arm. Pavel would have won the battle and slain his brother had not the soldiers of the castle realized what was happening and moved to protect Kripke. Pavel retreated and using a Trump, contacted his brother Bleys who agreed to harbor him and teleported Pavel to his location. Pavel then agreed to aid Bleys in his attempts to assault Yander and defeat Kripke and gathered a large group of warriors from Shadow and assembled a navy, while Bleys created an army on land. From here Pavel attempted to contact his brothers, looking for allies. Avel, although supporting Kripke, gave Pavel a promise of safe passage by sea, as did his brother Gérard. He is unable to contact Peter but when he attempts to reach Jon, he views him in a prison and Jon desperately asks Pavel to free him before his image disappears. Using a Trump, Pavel then attempts to contact his father Chronoron, who has been missing for centuries and makes contact with him. Chronoron encourages him to seize the throne but the contact is eventually lost. When he contacts Random, Random reveals that Kripke has contacted him and revealed the full extent of his defenses, which are vast and powerful. Furthermore, Random tells Pavel that Kripke has gained control over the mysterious Jewel of Judgment, which allows him to control the weather among other things. Despite Random's misgivings, Pavel remains resolute in his desire to attack Yander with Bleys.

As the invasion begins, Pavel travels with the navy by sea but finds Avel waiting for him with a superior force, apparently in violation of their agreement. Kripke then contacts Pavel by Trump, who reveals that he knew about his plans from Avel and the two engage in a mental duel which Pavel is unable to break from. After exchanging taunts, Pavel launches a full mental assault on Kripke, which defeats him and leaves him with the knowledge that Pavel is his superior. Pavel then joins in the battle although it is hopeless: Avel's forces are already destroying Pavel's navy and he escapes by using a Trump to move him to Bleys and his army. Bleys had been constantly assaulted by creatures of Shadow and the poor weather conditions that have been created by Kripke's usage of the Jewel of Judgment. Although they eventually reach Yander, their forces have dwindled and they barely fight their way up Kolvir, the mountain on which the Castle of Yander is situated. Bleys is ultimately pushed off a cliff, although Pavel throws him his pack of Trumps to allow him to escape the fall. Pavel then uses his few remaining forces and pushes through, eventually breaching to the castle itself, although, before he reaches the throne, his forces are surrounded, and he ultimately is captured.

Pavel is brought forth in chains to endure Kripke's coronation. Robert, who is at Kripke's side, instructs Pavel to hand the crown of Yander to Kripke, who will crown himself King of the one true world. Pavel instead crowns himself King of Yander, but he is quickly beaten by the guards and eventually throws the crown at Kripke. Kripke then crowns himself, and sentences Pavel to be imprisoned, and his eyes burned out.

In his prison beneath the city, Pavel is driven to near insanity, although the visits and smuggled gifts of his friend Lord Rein help him to maintain his spirit and his hope. After a year has passed in blindness and solitude, he is let out to eat at Kripke's table on the anniversary of the coronation before being thrown into the dungeons again. After years have passed, Pavel's eyesight begins to regenerate, and he begins an escape attempt by whittling the door with a spoon he stole from Kripke's table. Before he can escape in this manner, Qweryin the keeper of the Pattern, appears out of nowhere, having seemingly walked through the dungeon wall from a neighboring cell. He explains that entered Pavel's cell by drawing a picture on the dungeon wall and walking through it, and wishes to return in the same way. Pavel gives him the spoon in order to draw a Trump image on the wall, and persuades him to draw the Lighthouse of Cabra on the opposite wall. With this, Pavel projects himself out of his prison.

At the Lighthouse of Cabra he meets Jopin, the keeper of the lighthouse but he does not reveal his true identity to him. Jopin cares for Pavel and Pavel aids Jopin in his activities around the lighthouse. Once he is fully recovered, Jopin recognises Pavel, and shows him that the Vale of Garnath, previously a pleasant valley adjacent to Yander, has become warped and twisted evil place. Pavel takes Jopin's craft Butterfly and sails away, while sending a message to Kripke via a black bird, stating that he will return to claim the throne

Characters[]

The Royal family is headed by King Chronoron of Yander who is mysteriously absent . Kripke know holds the kingship .


  • Peter - The oldest surviving prince; uninvolved in the current struggle for the crown. The master tactician of the family and presumed to be dead by the rest of the family.
  • Pavel - The protagonist. A cross between a cruel rogue and a reluctant poet, his years on Earth seem to have softened him somewhat.
  • Kripke - The arrogant yet competent would-be king of Yander; he commands the loyalty of Robert, Avel and Gérard.
  • Avel - Calculating and realistic.
  • Bleys - Dashing and charming; Pavel's other ally in his fight against Kripke.
  • Jon - Like Chronoron, mysteriously unavailable.
  • Robert - Patrols the forrests of Losiniy with his massive hounds. A sinister hunter.
  • Gattler - Physically strongest of the nine, known for his loyalty and is liked by all although not know for intellegence.
  • Random - A sneaky rascal albeit Pavel's ally. A gambler and the youngest of Chronoron's children.
  • Florimel - More commonoy known as Flora. Currently residing on Shadow Earth. Not a candadite for succession.
  • Deirdre - Know for her good looks and kind heart. Favorite sibling of Pavel.
  • Shriona - Princess of Yander, daughter of Chronoron.Known to have magical abilites.
  • Ciwilla - Princess of Yander, daughter of Chronoron and Moins. Currently resides in Rebma.

Adaptations[]

A three part comic adaptation was done by Terry Bisson in 1996.
